concerns.text: Circular/Blocking Dependency: T022b (Global Covariance) and T022c (Mahalanobis) are in Phase 4 (US2) but depend on T024 (Filtering) and T027d (Model Selection) which are in Phase 2 (Foundational). T027d depends on T024. This creates a logical block where US2 cannot produce its core features (T022a/b) until the Model Selection (T027d) is complete, yet T027d requires the filtered data (T024) which is a prerequisite for US2. The 'Independent Implementation' goal of US2 is broken because it cannot run without the output of T027d (model_type flag) which is logically downstream of the data it needs to process.

Hidden Ordering Violation: T022c (Mahalanobis) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T027d (Model Selection) to check `model_type == 'rf'`. A task that conditionally executes based on a flag set by a blocking prerequisite in a different phase cannot be parallel-safe with other US2 tasks. It must be serialized after T027d.

Producer/Consumer Violation: T025a-core (Compute Per-Sample Stats) depends on T022a (Per-Sample Entanglement) and T024 (Filtered Data). However, T022a is in Phase 4 while T024 is in Phase 2. The task description says 'Merge features from T022a... Do NOT re-compute T020-T021'. This implies T022a must complete before T025a-core. If T022a is blocked by T027d (as per T022c logic), then T025a-core is also blocked, preventing US2 from being independently shippable.

Inconsistent Phase Labeling: T024 (Filtering) and T027d (Model Selection) are listed in Phase 2 (Foundational), but T022b (Global Covariance) and T022c (Mahalanobis) are in Phase 4 (US2). Since T022b depends on T024 and T022c depends on T027d, the 'Foundational' phase is incomplete without the US2 tasks, or the US2 tasks are not independent. The phase boundaries do not reflect the actual data-flow dependencies.
